html:
The Second Congo War, fought from 1998 to 2003, drew in nine African countries and many armed groups, and is often called Africa's world war.

When Laurent-Désiré Kabila turned against his Rwandan and Ugandan backers, they invaded again with new rebel groups. Angola, Zimbabwe and Namibia sent troops to save Kabila. The country was split into zones, and armies and militias looted gold, diamonds, timber and coltan.

A peace deal in 2002 led to a transitional government in 2003. Surveys estimated millions of deaths from 1998 to the late 2000s, most from hunger and disease among displaced people, though the figures are disputed. Fighting went on in the east in the Kivu conflict, after the First Congo War.
sum: The Second Congo War, fought from 1998 to 2003, drew in nine African countries and many armed groups, and is often called Africa's world war.
